title: Inventory of Lean Surface

canonical_node.axiom: The inventory file is a reader-facing map of the current Lean surface, listing core files, theorem families, integrity markers, and the strong-law mechanism layer.
definitions: Core files: Lean files containing theorem spines, integration layers, adversarial tests, coherence, fracture, fall, chi evaluator, Maxwell/Trinity, delayed-choice, and God-test formal layers.

Major theorem families: collections of theorems addressing coupling, chi product, signature discipline, field-control gates, coherence, entropy, restoration, fracture, fall, grace-floor, chi evaluator, pressure-gradient, fruit, Maxwell/Trinity, delayed-choice, God-marker, and adversarial rejection.
Integrity markers: compact checkpoint theorems that, if they compile, indicate a bundle of key definitions and theorem dependencies still holds together.
Strong-law mechanism layer: a file closing GAP-01 at the mechanism-gate level for Laws 1, 2, 9, and 10, adding GGate, MGate, FGate, CGate.
derivation: The inventory lists core files and their roles.
It identifies integrity markers as compact checkpoints.
It describes the strong-law mechanism layer and its gates.
It concludes that the inventory is a map, not a proof artifact.
canonical_node.action: The system should treat this inventory as a navigational index for the Lean surface, using it to locate files, theorem families, and markers, but not as a source of new theorems or proofs.
boundary: This document does not contain formal proofs or theorem statements.
It does not establish any mathematical or theological claim.
It does not define the semantics of the gates or markers beyond naming them.
It does not provide verification results or compilation status.
test: Check that each listed file exists and corresponds to the described role.
Check that each named marker theorem is present in the corresponding file.
Check that the listed theorem families are represented in the files.
Check that the strong-law mechanism layer file exists and contains the named gates and marker.

dg1_dependencies: The listed Lean files (Final_Lean4_From_Excel.lean, Theophysics_Core.lean, etc.)
The named marker theorems (core_pipeline_marker, chi_evaluator_marker, etc.)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a reader-facing map of the Lean surface, enabling navigation and orientation but adding no new formal capability.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existing Lean surface by documenting it without modification.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If removed, readers lose a convenient index but the Lean files and theorems remain unaffected.

overstatement_risks: Treating the inventory as a proof of the listed theorems' validity.
Assuming the listed files compile or are correct.
Interpreting the inventory as a formal specification of the gates or markers.
kill_conditions: If any listed file does not exist or does not match its described role.
If any named marker theorem is absent from its file.
If the inventory is used as a substitute for formal verification.
risk.lean_target: The inventory itself is not a Lean target; it is a documentation file. The Lean targets are the listed files and markers.

plain_summary: This document is an inventory of the Lean formalization surface, listing core files, theorem families, integrity markers, and a strong-law mechanism layer. It is a navigational map, not a proof artifact, and should be treated as such.
